hints.content: Let's perform each of the sequences and see if they map $\triangle XYZ$ onto $\triangle ABC$.

In Sequence A we perform a translation $2$ units to the right and $10$ units up...



[[☃ image 1]]

...then a reflection over the line $\overleftrightarrow{AC}$.



[[☃ image 2]]

We can see that this sequence does *not* map $\triangle XYZ$ onto $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: The first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Triangle A B C has point A at ten, ten, point B at eight, eight, and Point C at two, ten. The pre image of triangle X Y Z has point X at the origin, point Y at two, two, and point Z at eight, zero. The image of triangle X Y Z has point X at two, ten, point Y at four, twelve, and point Z at ten, ten. There is a green line that highlight the shift two units right and ten units up.

The first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Triangle A B C has point A at ten, ten, point B at eight, eight, and Point C at two, ten. The pre image of triangle X Y Z has point X at two, ten, point Y at four, twelve, and point Z at ten, ten. There is horizontal line on side AC that the leads to the image of triangle X Y Z which has has point X at two, ten, point Y at four, eight, and point Z at ten, ten.

hints.content:
In Sequence B we perform a translation $6$ units to the right and $6$ units up...



[[☃ image 1]]

...then a $180\degree$ rotation about point $B$.



[[☃ image 2]]

We can see that this sequence *does* map $\triangle XYZ$ onto $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: The first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Triangle A B C has point A at ten, ten, point B at eight, eight, and Point C at two, ten. The pre image of triangle X Y Z has point X at the origin, point Y at two, two, and point Z at eight, zero. The image of triangle X Y Z has point X at the six, six, point Y at eight, eight, and point Z at fourteen, six. There is a green line that highlight the shift six units right and six units up.

The first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Triangle A B C has point A at ten, ten, point B at eight, eight, and Point C at two, ten. The pre image of triangle X Y Z has point X at the six, six, point Y at eight, eight, and point Z at fourteen, six. The image of triangle X Y Z has point X at ten, ten, point Y at eight, eight, and Point Z at two, ten, which perfectly overlaps triangle A B C. There are half circle green arrows from the point X on the pre-image to point A and from point Z on the pre-image to point C.

hints.content:
In conclusion, only sequence B maps $\triangle XYZ$ onto $\triangle ABC$.

*Note:* There are many other possible combinations of transformations that would also map the figure onto the image.

question.content:
Triangles $\triangle XYZ$ and $\triangle ABC$ are congruent. The side length of each square on the grid is $1$ unit.



[[☃ image 1]]

**Which of the following sequences of transformations maps $\triangle XYZ$ onto $\triangle ABC$?**

Sequence A | Sequence B
:- | :-
A translation $2$ units to the right and $10$ units up, then a reflection over the line $\overleftrightarrow{AC}$. | A translation $6$ units to the right and $6$ units up, then a $180\degree$ rotation about point $B$.

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: The first quadrant of a coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Triangle A B C has point A at ten, ten, point B at eight, eight, and Point C at two, ten. Triangle X Y Z has point X at the origin, point Y at two, two, and point Z at eight, zero.
